newsitem.title: FRANCE: Fedex plans Sept start for CDG-Asian hub.
newsitem.headline: Fedex plans Sept start for CDG-Asian hub.

text.p: Federal Express, said it planned to launch a long-haul eastbound route from its Paris/Charles de Gaulle hub later this year as part of its round-the-world service.
Last year, FedEx confirmed CDG as its European hub, unveiling an ambitious, long-term investment programme at the Paris airport.

"While it's not 100 percent confirmed, we are looking at September 1997 as a start-up date for the new service with the likely routing CDG-Dubai-Indian sub-Continent (possibly Bombay)-Subic Bay (Philippines)," a FedEx official told Reuters.
The service would be probably be operated by MD11 and DC10 freighters, which FedEx already uses on routes between CDG and the U.S., the official said.
Meanwhile, FedEx's proposed Boeing 727F service between Paris/CDG and Tel Aviv is set to be launched early this summer.
David Bronzcek, FedEx vice president for Europe, Africa and the Middle East said during a recent private visit to Israel the company will make four flights a week beginning in June.
"A launch had been pencilled in for March but we didn't want to start-up without the operational side of things being absolutely right as is our normal policy," the official said.
"While routing has yet to be finalised, it's likely that the Tel Aviv service will be an extension of our existing Paris/CDG-Frankfurt 727F feeder."
The possibility of a stopover on the westbound leg to CDG from Tel Aviv, for example, in Istanbul, had been mooted but was still under consideration, the official added.
"The main priority of the return leg is to get Israel-orginating shipments to CDG and from there access to our worldwide network, via our DC10 and MD11 freighter services to the U.S.."
FedEx transports cargo to Israel on commercial airlines, including state-owned Israeli carrier, El Al.
While in Israel, Bronzcek met with El Al officials to discuss future co-operation.
Until now, it had not been worthwhile for FedEx to operate its own planes to and from Israel but this had changed with growing volumes of traffic.
Bronzcek would return to Israel in May to work out details of FedEx' expanded service to Israel, FedEx said in a statement earlier this week. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
